handoff: Review #1: changes requested, with 7 blocking findings. F1: a built-in agent named only on a step is not built (B13). F2: shipped text still names removed keys and the removed capability check (B52, B36). F3: migrate silently drops team limits it cannot place, and skips .json workflows (B43). F4: a slice with needs loads as corrupt and is recognised by regex on its message (D12). F5: config files are checked by hand instead of the file schemas, and the two disagree (D2). F6: an unreachable ntfy URL never names its file (B47). F7: test gaps at the agreed seams (B3, B14/B15, B35). Unit tests 1077/0, typecheck clean.

findings.title: Built-in agents without an entry are not built, so a step naming one fails at launch
findings.detail:
Spec B13: 'with built-in names usable without an entry'. buildPorts builds agents only for config.agent ∪ keys(config.agents). Only claude has a built-in entry. A workflow step with `agent: gemini` and no `agents.gemini` reaches launchSession, which throws "agent 'gemini' is not configured" (runtime/act/session.ts:41). W5 does not catch it (core/src/workflow.ts:45: an agent that is not listed is not checked).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Build every AGENT_NAMES adapter (or lazily any built-in name). Add an S1 test: a step with agent: codex and no agents entry launches Codex in FakeRunner.

findings.title: Shipped text still names removed config and the removed capability check
findings.detail:
B52: 'no doc ... names a removed key'. (1) An empty inbox in `norn status` prints "Label an issue `norn` (the config's `remote.label`)". The label is now fixed (B30). (2) packages/cli/assets/skills/norn-qa/SKILL.md:33 still says "A criterion needing a capability this session lacks (e.g. `browser`) ... a `pass` for it is refused". That describes the QV5a check D11 removed, and B36 says `norn done` accepts a pass from any agent. (3) The `norn config` summary (commands/config.ts:58) says 'user or repo file' and leaves out --local (D4). The S5 lint does not catch any of these.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Reword all three. Extend the S5 lint to cover `remote.label` and view/src strings.

findings.title: Migrate drops team limits it cannot place, and skips .json workflows, without listing them
findings.detail:
B43: drop every removed key 'and list each one with its value'. migrateWorkflows keeps only deadline/nudges/retries/stalled from team `limits`. Any other limit (e.g. attended_wait, now fixed per B27) is removed from the team file with no `removed` entry. Workflows stored as .json are filtered out with no report, so B41's 'every workflow gains defaults' fails for them and nobody is told.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: List each dropped limit with its value (e.g. 'removed limits.attended_wait: 5m: fixed at 2m'). Either migrate .json workflows or list them as not migrated. Add S1 cases.

findings.title: A slice with `needs` still loads with reason `corrupt` and is recognised by regex on the message
findings.detail:
D12: 'fails its frontmatter load with its own reason (not corrupt)'. frontmatter.ts returns `reason: "corrupt"`. core/inbox/items.ts:23 and cli/runtime/agent-unit.ts:102 tell it apart only by matching NEEDS_REMOVED_RE against the prose message (schema/criteria.ts:27). Any other caller that branches on reason === 'corrupt' treats it as corrupt, and rewording needsRemovedMessage silently turns the Unblock/migrate item back into 'corrupt'. AGENTS.md also says never to branch on prose.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Give ReadResult a distinct reason (e.g. 'needs_removed') or a code on FileError, and branch on that.

findings.title: Config files are validated by hand, not against the file schemas, and the two already disagree
findings.detail:
AGENTS.md: 'Validate with validate()/assertValid(); never hand-roll checks of these shapes'. D2: 'anything else failing the file's schema is config_invalid'. checkConfigFile/checkValue re-implement every rule, and the registered 'user-config'/'local-config'/'repo-config' schemas are used only to emit editor JSON. Verified drift: checkConfigFile('user', {notify:null}), {agents:null} and {agents:{claude:null}} report no problems, but validate('user-config', …) rejects each one ('must be object'). The editor schema (B50) flags files norn accepts. isUrl also copies the Url pattern. The branch edited AGENTS.md to name checkConfigFile, so the rule now contradicts itself.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Keep the moved and wrong-file passes. Then run validate('<kind>-config') on what is left and map its errors to config_invalid with the friendly messages. At minimum, add a parity test over sample files.

findings.title: An unreachable ntfy URL never names its file
findings.detail:
B47 example: 'an unreachable ntfy URL set in the user file → the error says to fix ~/.norn/config.yaml'. Only build-time failures name the file (wiring.ts:69–72). A valid but unreachable URL fails at send time, and env.ts swallows that error as best-effort, so no message names any file.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Attach the source file to send errors where they surface (trace event and doctor). For example, have doctor send a test notification and report a failure as FAIL config naming the file. Add the S1 test from the coverage table.

findings.title: Behaviour items without a test at the seam the Plan agreed
findings.detail:
Coverage table: B3 'two repos, one user home'. The test uses one repo and never checks 'in another repo, mode manual (user)'. B14/B15: only config entries are checked. No test checks the launched argv: --permission-mode auto with the model, and no extra flags after args: []. B35 (S2, unit): 'renew period'. No decide test renews at 3m20s or 6m40s; only the `norn config` display and the transcript cover it. Also, Testing decisions say 'none reaches into the resolver', but schema ids-config.test.ts calls resolveConfig directly and cli/test/unit/assets.test.ts calls checkConfigFile. B28 is tested through the internal hookWindowMs rather than through S4's loaded workflows.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add the S1 two-repo test, S1 FakeRunner argv tests for B14/B15, and S2 decide tests for renewal at the derived period. Move the resolver and checker tests to the S1 seam.

findings.title: Migrate takes the tick lock for the config part only after the layout move
findings.detail:
B45: 'refuse before changing anything when a precondition fails'. With the old layout, the layout is moved first and the lock is taken afterwards. A lock held at that moment refuses after files have already changed. The window is narrow.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Take the lock once, before the layout move, and hold it through the config part.

findings.title: Unrequested: migrate lowers a user max_agents above 9 to 9
findings.detail:
Sensible and listed in the report, but no Behaviour item asks for it (B53 asks for config_invalid).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Keep it and note it in the spec, or drop it.

findings.title: Silent catch in stripNeeds; doctor retry can rethrow
findings.detail:
stripNeeds has `catch { // no slices }`, which swallows every error, while its siblings rethrow anything but ENOENT via isErrno. In doctor.ts doctorPorts, the catch retries with notifiers: []. A failure from a non-notifier factory would rethrow and crash doctor instead of printing FAIL config (latent today). doctor.ts also keeps a module-level WeakMap cache, and Context.ports(overrides) overwrites builtPorts. claim.ts:28 comment still says max_checks.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Rethrow non-ENOENT errors. Make doctor's fallback catch per factory. Fix the stale comment.

findings.title: Duplicated slot port formula and moved-key tables
findings.detail:
SLOTS.port_base + slot*ports_per_slot appears in core decide/receipts.ts, store/worktree.ts and store/leases.ts. The moved/removed-key knowledge lives in schema MOVED, config-migrate REMOVED_NOTE and legacyConfig. In config-migrate.ts, `type Map` shadows the global Map.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: One slotPorts helper in schema; one moved-key table shared by the checker and migrate.
